raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--tool-call-parser glm47`, a request that supplies tools but explicitly sets `tool_choice="none"` still receives the GLM47 `full_assistant_ebnf` grammar.

That grammar describes a complete assistant turn. Reaching its terminal state finishes generation through the grammar path, which does not consult `ignore_eos`. An `ignore_eos=true` request can therefore stop at the model's end-of-turn token instead of reaching `max_tokens`, even though the request disabled tool calls.

### Behavior scope

| Request | Expected behavior | Ownership |
|---|---|---|
| No `tools` | Do not install the GLM47 tool-call grammar | Already fixed and tested by #39273 |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="none"` | Do not install the GLM47 tool-call grammar | Core fix in this PR |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="auto"` | Preserve the existing GLM47 grammar behavior | Regression coverage |
| `tools` + `tool_choice="required"` | Preserve the existing behavior | Regression coverage |
| `tools` + named tool choice | Preserve named-tool selection semantics | Regression coverage |
| Tools on `system`/`developer` messages | Include them in the active GLM47 grammar | Adjacent consistency fix requested during review |

### Relationship to #39273

The original version of this PR covered two cases:

1. requests with no tools; and
2. requests with tools plus `tool_choice="none"`.

While this PR was under review, #39273 independently added the `bool(effective_tools)` guard and a no-tools regression test as part of its GLM-5.3 work. Commit `f17f7705a5a67c137edf279edfdbd5460f2ceb6e` therefore already fixed case 1.

This branch was subsequently rebased onto main commit `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, which contains #39273. The duplicated no-tools production change and duplicated test were removed. The remaining core fix in this PR is case 2: tools are available, but the request explicitly disables tool calls with `tool_choice="none"`.

The no-tools history is retained here so reports that found the original analysis through this PR can follow that part of the fix to #39273.

## Modifications

Scope the GLM47 grammar to requests that provide tools and allow tool calls:

```python
glm_constraint = (
    self.tool_call_parser == "glm47"
    and bool(effective_tools)
    and request.tool_choice != "none"
    and not any(tool.function.strict for tool in effective_tools)
)
```

`auto`, `required`, and named-tool choices retain their existing grammar behavior. Other tool-call parsers are unchanged.

### Message-scoped tool consistency

`_effective_tools(request)` includes tools declared on `system` and `developer` messages. That effective set decides whether the GLM47 grammar is active, but the parser previously received only top-level `request.tools`. A request with message-scoped tools could therefore activate a grammar that omitted those functions.

The GLM47 parser now receives `effective_tools`. The regression test uses the real XGrammar parser and verifies message-scoped tools for `auto`, `required`, and named-tool choices, as well as the disabled `none` case.

### Test cleanup

- Keep the existing #39273 no-tools regression test.
- Remove the combined mocked no-tools/none test, which duplicated #39273 and the retained real-parser matrix.
- Remove the mocked auto test, which passed before this fix and only checked mock-result propagation.

Deliberately not changed:

- GLM47 grammar generation or grammar-terminal finish handling.
- Generic Jinja rendering of message-scoped tools, which affects multiple model families and needs separate cross-model coverage.
- Template compatibility for the `developer` role.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward code or kernel is changed. The checks below validate request semantics and grammar construction rather than model accuracy.

### Unit tests

Environment:

- Python 3.12.3
- pytest 9.1.1
- XGrammar available in the test image

Command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py \
  -k glm47 -v
```

On baseline `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, with the regression test applied but without the production fix:

```text
24 failed, 2 passed, 154 deselected, 16 warnings
```

The existing #39273 no-tools test passed. The new matrix failed for the message-scoped-tool cases and, importantly for this PR, for every `tool_choice="none"` subtest, including the case with a top-level tool.

With the fix applied:

```text
2 passed, 154 deselected, 16 warnings, 24 subtests passed
```

The complete serving-chat unit file was also run on the fixed snapshot:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py -v
```

```text
156 passed, 63 warnings, 126 subtests passed in 46.16s
```

### GLM-5.3 end-to-end reproduction

The E2E comparison specifically tested **tools plus `tool_choice="none"`**; it was not a no-tools test.

Source snapshots:

- Before: main commit `99463390f83a39776d452ba12199941b96a4f36f`
- After: the same source snapshot plus the production diff from local fix `c5649e50245567827c63ac9d9dc3fafb2334a00b`
- The relevant production code in that fix is identical to the subsequently rebased branch.

Hardware and model:

- 1 node with 8 x NVIDIA H200 GPUs
- Model path: `/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3`
- Served model name: `glm-5.3`
- Container tag: `sglang:dev-cu13-260921` 
- Launch requested TP=8 and DP-attention DP=8. The effective server log reported `tp_size=8`, `attn_dp_size=8`, and `dp_size=1`.
- The launch command passed `--chunked-prefill-size 32768`; the normalized server arguments logged an effective `chunked_prefill_size=4096`.
- `SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1` was set. 

Server command:

```bash
SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr41233-src/python \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/zhipuai/GLM-5.3 \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --context-length 102400 \
  --tp 8 \
  --dp 8 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```

Request, repeated five times against each server:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  --data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Answer exactly with the word OK and nothing else."
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "none",
  "temperature": 0,
  "seed": 42,
  "ignore_eos": true,
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "stop": null,
  "stream": false
}
JSON
```

Results:

| Snapshot | Completion tokens (5 runs) | Finish reason | `matched_stop` | Tool calls |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Baseline `99463390f8` | 66, 61, 47, 54, 67 | `stop` for all runs | 154827 for all runs | none |
| Fix `c5649e5024` | 300, 300, 300, 300, 300 | `length` for all runs | null for all runs | none |

Expected behavior: because the request explicitly disables tool calls and sets `ignore_eos=true`, no tool grammar should be installed and generation should continue until the 300-token cap. The fixed snapshot did so in all five runs.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark was run or claimed. Requests that continue to use the GLM47 grammar retain the same grammar-masking path. This PR only removes an inapplicable grammar from requests that explicitly disable tool calls.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed code according to the repository style.
- [x] Add regression coverage according to the unit-test admission rules.
- [x] Record the exact source snapshots and commands used for validation.
- [ ] Documentation update. Not needed for this internal request-routing fix.
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmark. No model-forward or performance change is claimed; targeted unit and E2E correctness results are provided above.

```bash
  --tp 8 \
  --dp 8 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```

Request, repeated five times against each server:

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  --data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Answer exactly with the word OK and nothing else."
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "none",
  "temperature": 0,
  "seed": 42,
  "ignore_eos": true,
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "stop": null,
  "stream": false
}
JSON
```

Results:

| Snapshot | Completion tokens (5 runs) | Finish reason | `matched_stop` | Tool calls |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Baseline `99463390f8` | 66, 61, 47, 54, 67 | `stop` for all runs | 154827 for all runs | none |
| Fix `c5649e5024` | 300, 300, 300, 300, 300 | `length` for all runs | null for all runs | none |

Expected behavior: because the request explicitly disables tool calls and sets `ignore_eos=true`, no tool grammar should be installed and generation should continue until the 300-token cap. The fixed snapshot did so in all five runs.


## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark was run or claimed. Requests that continue to use the GLM47 grammar retain the same grammar-masking path. This PR only removes an inapplicable grammar from requests that explicitly disable tool calls.

- [x] Record the exact source snapshots and commands used for validation.
- [ ] Documentation update. Not needed for this internal request-routing fix.
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmark. No model-forward or performance change is claimed; targeted unit and E2E correctness results are provided above.

detail.title: [Fix] glm47: Disable tool grammar for `tool_choice="none"`

files.patch:
@@ -1378,18 +1378,19 @@ def _process_messages(
         tool_call_constraint = None
 
         effective_tools = self._effective_tools(request)
-        # Only tool-bearing requests get the full-assistant EBNF: its terminal
-        # state finishes a request even under ignore_eos.
+        # A grammar reaching its terminal state ends generation regardless of
+        # `ignore_eos`, so only install it when the request allows tool calls.
         glm_constraint = (
             self.tool_call_parser == "glm47"
             and bool(effective_tools)
+            and request.tool_choice != "none"
             and not any(tool.function.strict for tool in effective_tools)
         )
         if glm_constraint:
             enable_thinking = (request.chat_template_kwargs or {}).get(
                 "enable_thinking"
             )
-            parser = FunctionCallParser(request.tools or [], self.tool_call_parser)
+            parser = FunctionCallParser(effective_tools, self.tool_call_parser)
             tool_call_constraint = parser.get_structure_constraint(
                 request.tool_choice,
                 parallel_tool_calls=request.parallel_tool_calls,

@@ -1346,6 +1346,69 @@ def test_jinja_tool_schema_fallback_to_flat_function(self):
             second_tools, [tool.function.model_dump() for tool in req.tools]
         )
 
+    def test_glm47_constraint_includes_message_tools(self):
+        """Constrain every active message tool, but none when tool use is disabled.
+
+        A terminal GLM47 grammar on ``tool_choice="none"`` ends generation early,
+        while omitting message-scoped tools rejects otherwise valid tool calls.
+        """
+        import xgrammar as xgr
+
+        self.template_manager.chat_template_name = None
+        self.template_manager.jinja_template_content_format = "string"
+        self.chat.tool_call_parser = "glm47"
+        self.tm.tokenizer.apply_chat_template.return_value = [1, 2, 3]
+        compiler = xgr.GrammarCompiler(
+            xgr.TokenizerInfo(
+                [bytes([i]) for i in range(256)], vocab_type=xgr.VocabType.RAW
+            ),
+            max_threads=1,
+        )
+        message_tool = {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {"name": "message_tool", "parameters": {"type": "object"}},
+        }
+        top_level_tool = {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {"name": "top_level_tool", "parameters": {"type": "object"}},
+        }
+        named = ToolChoice(function=ToolChoiceFuncName(name="message_tool"))
+        for role in ("system", "developer"):
+            for tools in (None, [], [top_level_tool]):
+                for choice in ("auto", "required", named, "none"):
+                    with self.subTest(role=role, tools=tools, choice=choice):
+                        request = ChatCompletionRequest(
+                            model="x",
+                            messages=[
+                                {"role": role, "content": "", "tools": [message_tool]},
+                                {"role": "user", "content": "Use message_tool."},
+                            ],
+                            tools=tools,
+                            tool_choice=choice,
+                            chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False},
+                        )
+                        result = self.chat._process_messages(
+                            request, is_multimodal=False
+                        )
+                        if choice == "none":
+                            self.assertIsNone(result.tool_call_constraint)
+                            continue
+                        self.assertIsNotNone(result.tool_call_constraint)
+                        kind, ebnf = result.tool_call_constraint
+                        self.assertEqual(kind, "full_assistant_ebnf")
+                        grammar = compiler.compile_grammar(xgr.Grammar.from_ebnf(ebnf))
+                        for name, allowed in (
+                            ("message_tool", True),
+                            ("top_level_tool", bool(tools) and choice != named),
+                            ("unknown_tool", False),
+                        ):
+                            matcher = xgr.GrammarMatcher(grammar)
+                            accepted = (
+                                matcher.accept_string(f"<tool_call>{name}</tool_call>")
+                                and matcher.is_completed()
+                            )
+                            self.assertEqual(accepted, allowed, name)
+
     def test_xgrammar_tag_omits_reasoning_when_parser_owns_it(self):
         """ReasonerGrammarBackend owns the thinking prefix when a parser is set."""
         self.template_manager.chat_template_name = None

Thanks for fixing this, I encountered this issue as well. I found one adjacent case while testing a local patch: `_effectuve_tools(request)` includes tools supplied in messages, so the new guard enables the GLM47 grammar for then. But `FunctionCallParser(request.tools or [], self.tool_call_parser)` still receives an empty list when `request.tools is None`, leaving those functions out of the grammar.

Would you consider passing `effective_tools` to `FunctionCallParser`?

Thanks, Addressed in 187304c0ef: the GLM47 `FunctionCallParser` now receives `effective_tools`, rather than only top-level `request.tools`, so the grammar includes tools declared on `system` and `developer` messages as well.

I added `test_glm47_constraint_includes_message_tools`, covering message-scoped tools with no/top-level tools and `auto`, `required`, named, and `none` tool choice. The related serving, protocol, and function-call unit suites pass locally (441 tests, 181 subtests).
Thanks! The PR looks good to me.

@YouNeedCryDear  @nvpohanh  thanks for review, I will address the above issues.

@YouNeedCryDear @nvpohanh 

Updated the branch after review.

- I rebased it onto `4b384df0c94dbd0fe30627c27c98c0441b4ebd96`, which already contains #39273 (`f17f7705a5`). That absorbs the no-tools fix from #39273 and leaves this PR focused on the remaining `tools + tool_choice="none"` case, plus the previously reviewed message-scoped-tool consistency fix.
- I removed the two redundant tests called out in review and kept the real-parser matrix.
- I added the required black-box regression docstring.
- The unit and E2E results in the description remain tied to the exact source snapshots on which they were run; I did not relabel them as results from a newer main.

I did not rebase again after those tests. As a private merge-safety check, I compared `4b384df0` with current upstream main `3e13f1b2`: neither changed file was modified in the intervening 60 commits, and `git merge-tree` reports a clean merge for the updated candidate. By contrast, the old pre-#39273 PR head conflicts in both files, which is why the earlier rebase was retained.

btw, related #42984 updates the same GLM47 grammar path for always-thinking templates. The two fixes address separate and complementary request semantics:

- this PR controls whether the grammar is enabled and passes effective_tools to the parser;
- #42984 determines the grammar’s thinking mode from the detected template configuration.

When both changes are integrated, the tool_choice != "none" guard, FunctionCallParser(effective_tools, ...), and the reasoning_config.always_on handling should all be preserved. I reviewed the two diffs for logical compatibility; the combined changes have not been runtime-tested.
